clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old woman presented with sudden-onset abdominal pain, metabolic lactic acidosis, leukocytosis, and elevated serum phosphate. Initial abdominal contrast-enhanced CT showed no bowel ischemic signs. The patient developed shock one hour after admission. Mesenteric angiography was ordered but not documented. Emergency laparotomy six hours after admission revealed discontinuous necrosis of the ileum and colon despite a pulsatile superior mesenteric artery. Surgical resection of the necrotic bowel segments with ileal resection, subtotal colectomy, and jejunostomy was performed. Histopathological examination was not reported, and no physical examination findings or detailed clinical course post-surgery were documented.
